subject: biology
title: Antagonistic Pairs
welcome_lead: Flex your biceps and learn why muscles always work together in pulling pairs.
meta_desc: KS3 Biology adventure on muscles working in antagonistic pairs.
final_note: You can now explain why muscles must work in pairs to move a limb both ways.

concepts.def: When a muscle shortens and pulls.
When a muscle returns to normal length.
Two muscles that work against each other.

walkthroughs.body_html: Muscles can contract (shorten) but they cannot push. So one muscle alone can only move a bone one way. Another muscle is needed to move it back.
The biceps contracts to bend the arm. To straighten the arm, the biceps relaxes and the triceps contracts. They form an antagonistic pair.
Antagonistic pairs work all over your body — at the knees, ankles, fingers and jaw. One muscle pulls one way; its partner pulls the other.
